The  COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa is being monitored through the National COVID-19 Data Dashboard, which provides real-time and historical information on the outbreak.  To better understand the COVID-19 situation, data analysis techniques have been employed to forecast hospitalization rates and detect spatial and temporal patterns of infection.  Specifically, a Bayesian hierarchical model has been used to forecast COVID-19-related hospitalizations, while another Bayesian model and spatial statistics have been used to analyze the COVID-19 situation across different geographic regions.  Our research showcases the benefits and constraints of utilizing these methods to facilitate more informed decision-making for addressing the COVID-19 crisis.

Freiman's 3k-4 theorem generally posits that if subsets A and B, of size k and comprised of integers, share a sumset with a size near 2k, then A and B exhibit considerable similarity to arithmetic progressions. In this paper, we aim to enhance this by limiting the number of possible summands available from subset B. Our findings demonstrate that if subsets A and B, of size k, meet the following conditions: for every triple of elements (a, b, c) such that a + b + c = 0 with at most one element from B, it follows that A and B resemble arithmetic progressions. To achieve this, we employ techniques from Freiman and Stepanov and utilize an enhanced version of the polynomial method known as Cayley's method.

In medical contexts, particularly for diagnosing certain conditions, different types of data are often produced which can aid diagnosis. For instance, in ophthalmology, two kinds of information are created that may help in identifying glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy: intraocular pressure measurements and fundus images. Our study investigates the effectiveness of combining these distinct data types for improved classification accuracy of retinal diseases and eye pressure. Using public datasets, specifically the RIMON-GL and IMAGE-GL for glaucoma and the MESSIDOR for diabetic retinopathy, the performance of separate models analyzing each data source was compared to models integrating all data. Our results demonstrate that combining data types yields enhanced classification outcomes, and further analysis via SHAP revealed the contribution of each data type to the overall model.

X-ray images contain subtle characteristics that aid machine learning models in identifying COVID-19 patients. These distinct features improve image classification accuracy by enabling systems to recognize specific indicators of the disease. However, there is uncertainty as to whether these characteristics truly represent physical symptoms of COVID-19 on X-rays. To address this uncertainty, researchers have developed the COVID-XR-IT, a web-based tool that allows radiologists to annotate X-ray images and confirm the presence of COVID-19-related features. By analyzing rations of X-ray images labeled as having pneumonia or fluid accumulation, researchers have discovered that these features are correlated with ICU admissions. This finding suggests that these features may be useful in predicting severe cases of COVID-19 and guiding ICU admissions. The COVID-XR-IT tool is freely accessible at https://radiology.tau.ac.il/~roif/COVID-2019/ to facilitate ongoing research and validation of X-ray features.

We analyze the transmission eigenvalue problem for the Helmholtz equation in a spherically symmetric, positive-definite medium, where we prove that transmission eigenfunctions localize near the medium's boundaries. Our proof, based on an alternative approach, also provides conditions under which transmission eigenvalues cannot occur, offering a problem-free problem. Additionally, we validate the principles of time-reversal invariance and spatial reflection invariance numerically.

To expand a dialogue system's capabilities, discovering new intent categories from user inputs is essential for seamless and intuitive interactions. However, most approaches are limited by a requirement for labeled data, which is often time-consuming to obtain and may not adequately reflect a user's true goals. In response to this challenge, we develop a cutting-edge approach that leverages pre-training and contrastive learning to identify new intent categories from both unlabeled and labeled data without requiring any annotations. Our method starts by pre-training the model on a large amount of unlabeled data to enhance its overall understanding of the dialogue system. Next, we employ a contrastive learning framework to fine-tune the model on labeled data, utilizing a unique method to compare user inputs and pinpoint categories that are similar to existing ones. Our proposed approach is tested on datasets drawn from the Amazon dataset of customer reviews, dialogue datasets, and simulated conversations with virtual characters. Our results show that the model outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in identifying new intent categories across all three data sources, highlighting its versatility and robustness.
The universal simplicial bundle G~X is indeed a simplicial group.
In our analysis, we demonstrate that a finite group of order $r$ possesses no more than $$7.3722\cdot r^{\frac{\log_2r}{4}+1.5315}$$ subgroups.

This study re-examines the Adler-Bobenko-Suris H2 equation. The equation has a direct linear relationship with the Cauchy matrix scheme. The research derives the underlying Lax pair, Lax representation, Bäcklund transformation, and its associated linear problem. The analysis also obtains the higher order Lax pair.

This paper delves into the source of high false positive rates in Visual Relationship Detection (VRD). During training, we discovered that the relationship proposal distribution is skewed, with the majority of incorrect relationships being easily identified due to poor object detection. As a result, low-frequency difficult proposals are given excessive emphasis in the VRD model. Our proposed solution directly tackles this imbalance by generating a covering distribution for all possible object and relationship proposals. The covering distribution is then broken down into multiple low-dimensional subspaces. Adaptive weights are assigned to each subspace based on the corresponding proposal distribution. Our approach significantly improves VRD performance. At test time, we introduce a novel difficulty-aware decision-making mechanism that enables the VRD model to make more challenging judgments when needed. Our approach yields notable reductions in the one-shot and few-shot full-image top-1 accuracy false positive rate for the COCO and Visual Genome datasets.

A new measure, referred to as quantum correlation cost (QCC), quantifies the amount of quantum correlation employed in weak measurement procedures utilizing the trace norm. It's demonstrated that the QCC is directly linked to the trace-norm-based quantum discord (TQD) by a factor dependent on weak measurement strength. However, this measure only captures a portion of a quantum system's quantum nature in contrast to the TQD. Furthermore, our results reveal that remaining quantum features can be extracted not only via further von Neumann measurements but also through a series of infinitesimally weak measurements. We exemplify these outcomes using a Bell-diagonal state.

Artificial intelligence systems capable of simulating human social interactions are referred to as social AI. While past research has mostly concentrated on producing intelligent actions for agents, there's little knowledge on developing mechanisms that define each agent's social relationships. Consequences such as actions are observable, but social relationships remain unseen, posing a challenge for learning models that can accurately capture these elusive connections. In contrast to existing methodologies that learn from imperfect data, this study focuses on developing a model capable of accurately representing social relationships, even when they are not directly visible. Our proposed method, which we will call Graph RL, simulates a multi-agent environment where the goal is to produce beneficial actions, and the model learns to predict social relationships by analyzing the effects of actions, which are accessible through video footage. Our model outperforms the current state-of-the-art in producing accurate social relationship models, and the models generated by our system are applicable in a range of practical tasks, such as social interaction analysis and prediction.

Capturing long-range relationships in scene understanding tasks is a crucial goal in computer vision. While current models are effective in this area, they often struggle with representing global context due to the limited capabilities of local graph neural networks. We propose a new architecture, called dynamic graph message passing networks, that surpasses the limitations of local graph neural networks and excels in various scene understanding tasks. Our approach starts by encoding each feature as a node in a graph, with the graph structure evolving over time. These nodes receive messages from neighboring nodes, with the message passing process enabling the graph to connect each feature with others crucial for comprehension of the entire image. Our experiments demonstrate the superiority of our model over state-of-the-art models in line detection, object detection, and semantic segmentation. The novel framework is simple to implement and produces graphs suitable for visualizing relationships within the image. Our findings convey a significant insight: effectively capturing dynamic relationships among image components is essential for scene understanding.

Optimizing hardware efficiency in digital circuits, the Multiple Constant Multiplication problem seeks the most resource-efficient way to compute $y = k_1c_1 + \dots + k_nc_n$, where the $k_i$ are small positive constants and $c_i$ are variable inputs. To overcome current limitations, this research proposes an algorithm that finds the most efficient constant multiplication methods with multiple factors ranging from 2 to a specified maximum, ensuring they all produce consistent outputs. While previous approaches focused on individual multiplications, this new method aims to minimize the overall hardware cost by standardizing the design of these multiplications. Although comprehensive results with $k_{max} = 2$ exist, this research aims to extend these findings to scenarios with larger constants, offering a systematic method to accurately estimate the cost associated with these multiplications and ultimately improving circuit design outcomes.

The intersection of quantum computing and deep neural networks has recently given rise to a growing research field, known as quantum deep learning. Despite previously being separate entities, advancements have revealed that quantum circuits share parallels with artificial neural networks, paving the way for widespread adoption. This paper delves into the foundational aspects and core principles of quantum deep learning, highlighting key breakthroughs along the way. It also explores the challenges inherent in quantum deep learning research from multiple viewpoints, followed by a discussion of prospective future directions and practical applications.

The radio frequency (RF) accelerator technology continues to be fundamental in 
high-energy physics (HEP) experiments, where significant progress has been 
made over the past decade in advancing the field. This progress could soon lead 
to upgraded existing facilities, enhancements to facilities still under 
construction, and the creation of new facilities. The common goal behind this 
advancement involves introducing new types of accelerating structures and the 
materials used to build them, which require precise electron source 
technology, high-power electronics, and advanced computational modeling 
tools. The advancements in the field of accelerator technology could also have 
beneficial effects on other areas of HEP, other physics disciplines, and 
industrial applications.

In the near future, physicists anticipate that the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) will discover new physics. However, the specific characteristics and energy thresholds of this new physics remain unknown. It's probable that insights gleaned from LHC data will require supplementary information obtained from a lepton collider to conduct a thorough investigation. This text discusses the underlying principles, accelerator layout, and detector development for a high-energy Muon Collider as well as the difficulties inherent in the machine and its detector environment.

We have determined the dispersion relations for relativistic fluid modes in various configurations - scalar, vector, and tensor - and found the differences between their behavior in divergence-based and relaxation-time-approximation models. Our comparison also shows how these theoretical models relate to specific kinetic theory kinetic distributions, particularly for a massless Visseras distribution in the divergence-based model and a $q$-deformed Fermi-Dirac distribution with $q \simeq 1 - 9/8q_{\mathrm{max}}$ in the relaxation-time-approximation model.

Our research assesses whether the cosmic background of Hawking radiation from primordial black holes could be the source behind the observed excess radio signals in the Fast Radio Burst spectrum. We found the intensity of this emission is heavily dependent on the PBH's mass and the surrounding gas density, with an optimal range of mass (10^15-10^17 grams) for radio wave generation. In the optimal range, radio radiation is predominantly produced by interactions between Hawking photons and hydrogen atoms. For a mass of 10^15 grams, the energy released can substantially contribute to the Fast Radio Burst excess, whereas a 10^17 gram mass primarily results in a minor addition. Notably, PBHs in the 10^17 gram mass range can still effectively generate the observed intensity, even if their contribution is minor.

Introducing the Virtual Secure Platform (VSP), a pioneering solution that brings together multi-party computation (MPC) and system architecture to secure computation. The VSP leverages the TFHE scheme, a computation-friendly method that enables MPC to scale with constant overhead, making it suitable for secure data processing without requiring trusted parties. The VSP platform consists of a five-stage pipeline processor architecture designed to streamline MPC operations, including instruction fetch, decode, execute, memory access, and write back stages. The architecture uses a little-endian approach to decode instructions and incorporates a innovative method to execute additions and comparisons with MPC. The VSP platform features a customized pipeline architecture tailored for instruction fetch, register file management, and memory access with support for both secure and insecure caches. Introducing the VSP is akin to integrating a secure layer of protection within a computation platform, allowing users to upload data without revealing their secrets. The VSP platform will play a pivotal role in advancing research in secure computation through its integration into educational and experimental processes.

Research on finding general-valued constraint satisfaction problems that are NP-hard but have the potential for efficient approximation algorithms within a factor of $n^\epsilon$ has been a major focus in the APX approximation community. A notable case in point is the minimum $k$-cut problem, which involves partitioning vertices into $k$ sets, with a simple polynomial-time $O(k)\log k$-approximation algorithm available. Recently, P. Allen et al. discovered a PTAS for the sparse graph version of this problem. This paper builds on the work of Allen et al. and generalizes their result to value domains of arbitrary size. Our approach is rooted in sampling and relies on rephraseable and conflict-free properties of the constraint satisfaction problem, as well as techniques such as multi-objective approximation, which were introduced in our earlier research. By integrating these tools, our work extends the known PTAs to sparse graphs with arbitrary value domains and potentially more complex CSP instances.

Pre-trained language models possess the ability to capture syntactic information, as demonstrated in previous studies. This work has further explored this phenomenon, showing that pre-trained language models capture enough of the necessary syntax for a parser to achieve state-of-the-art parsing accuracy with minimal or no training data. Specifically, using the GLUE benchmark, it was found that accurate parsing can be achieved with fewer than 1000 annotated sentences using the FParse parser, or without any training data using the ParseEval parser. The FParse model with fewer-shot data even outperformed fully-trained strong baselines on certain metrics. A new pre-trained syntax-aware language model, named Syntax-T5, is also introduced, which enhances its ability to capture syntactic information by incorporating the FParse predictions.

High-definition hyperspectral images possess the unique capability to distinguish between diverse material compositions within each pixel, leveraging high-resolution spectral signatures. However, their application in the automotive sector is hindered by the absence of efficient algorithms capable of accurately categorizing urban landscapes. This study presents a innovative approach for training a city material classifier using only hyperspectral image data. Nevertheless, to enhance performance, it incorporates manually-annotated RGB images in an post-training phase via a contrastive loss mechanism. This technique leverages existing cityscape datasets annotated in a semi-automatic fashion and relies on an automatic segmentation method that doesn't rely on RGB channels. Consequently, it facilitates the development of hyperspectral image applications within automotive systems, while also accelerating training processes through a few-shot methodology. Experimental findings validate the proposed approach, exhibiting a mIoU accuracy of 41.1% within a 5-shot framework and progressing to an mIoU of 60.3% after incorporating manual RGB data for refinement.

This study reveals intriguing evidence of a complex internal rotation pattern within a less massive and less luminous star that has evolved into a giant. Typically, lower and intermediate mass stars retain their rapid rotation rates during their main sequence phase. However, once these stars expand into giants, we expect a rapid decline in surface rotation due to the separation of components with different moments of angular momentum. Contrary to expectations, this research discovers that the star's surface rotation rate actually increased significantly as it evolved. The research suggests two plausible explanations for this phenomenon: either the star underwent a interaction with a giant planet that was destroyed, or it developed an internal mechanism capable of effectively transferring angular momentum within its structure. The research suggests that dynamo-driven convective turbulence within the star's outer layer could be the source of this unusual internal rotation pattern. The mass of the engulfed planet is suggested to be approximately 1 Jupiter mass based on the analysis. The research concludes that this star's surface rotation rate stabilized after the planet interaction or internal adjustment took place.

In algorithmic literature, the underlying computation model is typically implicit and assumed to be based on the RAM model. Despite being widely adopted, the RAM model lacks a solid theoretical foundation, characterized by inconsistent definitions of machine instructions, word length, and address space, hindering comparisons of theoretical results obtained under different assumptions. Furthermore, operations such as multiplication and division are often treated as basic instructions, even though they are not geometrically related to the bit length of the input or output. The standard analysis ignores the cost of accessing machine words, contradicting the standard geometric cost model used in other computation settings, such as external sorting or fractional cascading. The cost functions are frequently manipulated arbitrarily, such as applying the square root or logarithm to the access cost to obtain more favorable results. The examples and counterexamples in this work adhere to a strict computation model where all operations are performed in the geometric RAM model and the cost of arithmetic operations is proportional to the bit length of the operands. The study establishes a comprehensive framework of feasible and infeasible functions, revealing a diverse structure of possible computation costs and raising new theoretical questions.

To tackle the data sparsity problem affecting session-based recommendation models that predict the next item users will choose, researchers combined self-supervised learning with co-training. They proposed an enhanced framework by leveraging a session-based graph to create informative, not artificially sparse, data for these models. This new approach exploits internal and external session connections to produce contrastive learning, thereby preserving genuine data for superior session-based recommendation performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate the success of this innovative method in achieving state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmark datasets.

This research presents a novel method for generating LCD codes using group rings and a standard transformation that maps group ring components to subring components. The possible images of group ring components form the basis for generating LCD codes, with group reversible LCD codes being an ideal outcome when these images maintain symmetry. A sufficient condition is presented for a group ring component to induce a group reversible image under mapping. A variety of group ring and group reversible LCD codes examples are provided, including cyclic and constacyclic codes, to demonstrate the effectiveness of this mapping approach.

We examine differential forms on an algebraic compactification of the graph complexes, defined by Aganagic and Keating [arXiv:2103.06708], and identify the invariant subspace consisting of these forms. This special subspace has the property of being divisible by the Chen-Leinster Euler idempotent and we identify its dimension to be 2 times that of the Chen-Leinster ideal. Furthermore, it's shown that the form of graph differential invariants, previously defined by the second two authors [arXiv:1910.01053], provides an explicit, basis-like set of forms, and there is additional space for invariant differential forms. We also examine the connection between the invariant space and Feynman integrals, noting that it is specifically related to weight w triple zeta values, and it has basis-like sets of forms represented by single, irreducible, unlabelled, 1-loop graph Feynman integrals.

In various object categorization tasks, particularly in visually complex conditions, it has been demonstrated that recurrent neural networks (RNNs) can outperform feedforward models.  This research aimed to uncover the specific role of recurrence in visual object categorization by analyzing RNNs.  We discovered through representational similarity analysis that the final categorization decisions made by recurrent models are heavily influenced by category-orthogonal object features that play a more significant role in processing complex stimuli.  This effect is particularly pronounced in conditions with high visual interference.  Our results can be explained by a more in-depth processing mechanism in recurrent models involving the suppression of visually complex, category-orthogonal features during the final decision-making process.  This processing mechanism is crucial in optimizing performance for final categorization decisions.

Despite significant progress in understanding topological phases with Hermitian systems, the landscape of topological phases in non-Hermitian systems remains elusive due to the proliferation of new phase types that defy conventional topology. Many researchers have proposed that correlations could restore a set of traditionally understood topological phases. This paper presents a method for determining the correlation topological phase of one-dimensional Hermitian and non-Hermitian systems that exhibit integer values for both the Chern number and the winding number. Through an examination of specific models, it is demonstrated that systems may possess high-order correlations that reveal the presence of topological phases inaccessible through second-order correlation analysis. Furthermore, it is shown that the topological properties of systems with interactions can differ substantially from those of systems with analogous non-interacting counterparts.

Recently, Golay complementary matrices have gained popularity due to their utility in omnidirectional precoding techniques. This research extends Golay complementary matrices to higher-dimensional spaces known as multi-dimensional Golay complementary arrays and presents novel construction methods for pairs and quadruples of GCA sets. A specific focus is placed on GCA sets consisting of four quadruples, with a provided example of such a set for the case where four GCA sets are required and each set contains matrices of size $4\times4$.

Research on Higgs boson production is conducted, combining CMS data from 13 TeV LHC and previous 7 and 8 TeV LHC data in the four-lepton final state. Updated measurements on Higgs boson decay widths and anomalous HVV interactions are performed, incorporating the concept of interference between different production methods such as off-resonance decay, virtual particle effects and potential new interactions. While no clear evidence of new interactions was found, refined forecasts are made for future four-lepton studies.

Incorporating dimensionality reduction techniques, researchers address the complexities of analyzing numerous spectral bands within bi-temporal hyperspectral images. This study proposes a cutting-edge approach using a novel deep convolutional autoencoder that fuses features across hierarchical levels and receptive fields. By utilizing an unsupervised change detection technique, it overcomes the limitations of other label-dependent methods. By integrating various techniques to extract changes from the images, it significantly outperformed current state-of-the-art methods in unsupervised change detection across diverse datasets.

The set of square numbers is being denoted by $\sqsubset$. This square number complement has the form $C(\sqsubset, k)$, where it includes all positive integers $n$ such that the sum of $n$ with at least one square number from each of the sets ${\rm sq}(k)$, for $1 \leqslant k \leqslant 8$, is a member of that set. Based on the work by Chaika and Liu from 2019, it was found that the density of this complement is higher than that of its additive counterpart, denoted by $\mathcal{C}(\sqsubset, k)$. We have derived the density of $C(\sqsubset, 8)$ to be $0.17355\ldots$, and provided a lower bound for the density of $C(\sqsubset, k)$ for each $9 \leqslant k \leqslant 80$, which ranges from $4.776\ldots \times 10^{-23}$ for $C(\sqsubset, 80)$ to $0.149999999999999907$ for $C(\sqsubset, 9)$. Furthermore, we have demonstrated that the density of $C(\sqsubset, k)$ approaches $1$ as $k$ approaches from above $

Quantum tunneling is an inherent process that occurs in silicon when manipulated electronically. By employing lattice-matched insulating barriers made of diamond, boron, and aluminum, researchers can create single-spin qubits within the silicon lattice. These experiments integrate electron tunneling with precise control over valley degrees of freedom, enabling the investigation of valley interference and exchange interactions at the atomic level. Experiments have demonstrated direct evidence of valley interference, as well as valley and spin exchange, as functions of tunneling amplitude. Furthermore, researchers developed model calculations that explain observed phenomena and predict untested effects, ultimately informing the design of robust silicon quantum processors.

Optimization techniques have various applications in scheduling, SMT solver, and scheduling problems. However, researching new o-techniques is becoming increasingly challenging due to the inherent complexity of their mathematical foundations and the difficulty in testing enhancements due to limited implementation tools. Our solution, a open-source tool known as LibOPT, facilitates rapid prototyping of various types of optimization techniques by providing a comprehensive framework for development, implementation, and experimental evaluation. Our evaluation, using problem sets from MCNC and UCLAM, showcases the effectiveness of LibOPT's performance and efficiency and highlights its superiority in certain scenarios. LibOPT is comprised of multiple modular components, including a development framework, search methods, exact methods, and validation techniques, and its latest version now also includes support for stochastic optimization techniques and multi-objective optimization techniques. Its comprehensive documentation is available at: http://libopt.org.

Given an algebraic variety X that has a transitive action from the group Aut(X), the highest degree of transitivity of this action is called the transitivity degree. This degree is denoted by the maximum value of m for which Aut(X) acts transitively m times on X. In cases where Aut(X) is m-transitive for any positive value of m, we define the transitivity degree to be infinite. This study involves determining the transitivity degree for specific varieties, such as quasi-affine toric varieties, and homogeneous spaces, while exploring related open problems and conjectures.

In non-commutative space-time deformations, the definition of identical particles breaks down. These models are described by non-abelian space symmetries represented by a four-momentum group. Our approach defines the Hilbert space for $N$ identical particles as the symmetric $N$-fold tensor product of the single-particle state space. The states space is characterized by its dimension, which relates to the non-commutative space size. The symmetry operation for exchanging the $i$-th and $j$-th particles does not simply swap labels but applies a specific transformation. This transformation is consistent with the non-commutative permutation group. The interaction of particles is defined by an invariant state under the four-momentum group. The initial, final, and scattering states are initially defined but the existence of an invariant state remains unverified.

We've employed the two-photon absorption edge transient current technique to investigate the charge transport properties in high purity single-phase diamond, achieving a measured mobility value of $1.07 \pm 0.04 \, \mathrm{cm}^2/\mathrm{V}\cdot \mathrm{s}$ that exceeds previously attained levels by more than an order of magnitude. This technique combines a pulsed laser and precise electronic equipment to investigate how carriers behave in diamond, with two-photon absorption serving as a non-intrusive method to generate electron-hole pairs. Notably, the charge mobility measured has not been influenced by interface effects. Our study also included numerical simulations that confirm the measured mobility, thereby validating our findings. By achieving such a high level of control over material purity, our findings open the door for utilizing diamond as a lustrous, transparent p-n junction device material across various wavelengths of light.

Social media platforms are subject to the same laws as traditional publications, specifically those safeguarding against hate speech and discriminatory language. The rise of artificial intelligence has made automated misbehavior classification more feasible. This research introduces a new dataset comprising social media texts from two categories: hate speech and prejudice, focusing on texts targeting women due to misogyny. The study utilizes deep learning models to achieve high accuracy rates of 86.66% for binary classification and 71.94% top-1 accuracy for multi-class classification, with a particular emphasis on employing Gated Recurrent Neural Networks (GRU) that demonstrate superior performance. The findings reveal that using Entity-RoBERTa as a feature extractor resulted in a 12% accuracy improvement, prompting further exploration into the effectiveness of pre-trained language models such as BERT, RoBERTa, and BART. The code is accessible on the GitHub repository: https://github.com/AlaaElsherifN/NeArMeP.

This study centres around the solvability of a distinct class of fractional backward stochastic differential equations that take into account past influences within their generators, under Lipschitz condition it's demonstrated that the existence and uniqueness of such equations are assured. Furthermore, a key comparison theorem has been formulated.

We examine if controllers obtained using model-based Reinforcement Learning, which employs an environment model to find the optimal policy, remain robust and adaptable when dealing with slight environmental variations. Building upon the concept from PILCO, a method for probabilistic policy search, our research demonstrates that constraining the uncertainty in the Gaussian Process model's dynamics has a beneficial effect. As a result, controllers become less sensitive to disturbances and more versatile. Further, our findings show that by incorporating a regularization term into the cost function, which limits excessive control efforts, the robustness of these controllers is enhanced. Using open-source simulation software with the Robotics Challenge Benchmark, we verify the applicability of these methods in a variety of robotic tasks.

Several key network communication challenges such as caching and computation are interconnected. A centralized caching approach seeks to mitigate network strain during peak times by pre-storing popular content. Concurrently, distributed computation aims to optimize computation time by leveraging multiple servers' combined processing power. Our work unifies caching and computation schemes through a generalized framework. We initially model a general memory-computation pair, from which popular content is randomly selected, and the system computes a function of this content, which may vary or remain the same across different functions. Our framework thus encompasses both caching and computation schemes. We derived lower bounds on the communication rate and the computation degree under specific constraints. These bounds are shown to be optimal in several instances. Notably, a universal file allocation strategy was identified, enabling optimal performance across a range of popular content. Furthermore, a generalized form of linear equation resolution was developed to prove lower bounds on the computation degree. We then applied this framework to a popular problem in related fields - the index coding problem.

We establish a formalization of the Scott model in univalent type theory, adopting a constructive and predicative framework. To capture the essence of non-terminating processes in PCF, we employ the lifting monad from topos theory, which has been adapted for univalent type theory by Escard\'o and Knapp. Our work confirms that using the lifting monad provides a viable way to handle partiality within univalent type theory, and we also demonstrate that a predicative and constructive Scott model is achievable. Notably, we avoid reliance on choice or decision principles for this outcome.

Hanzer and Muić's work on degenerate Eisenstein series cancellations has been built upon, 
extending their method and outcome to a specific set of Eisenstein series, 
specifically those formed from the combinations of two Speh representations 
for SL($2n$, $\mathbb{Q}$ at level two. 
The aim of this work is to reproduce the cancellation formula, 
inviting a exploration of the underlying combinatorial process. 
We observe that the general procedure of cancellation involves more complexity 
in comparison to the initial investigation of Hanzer and Muić. 
However, under specific conditions of intra-primeness and levels similarity, 
the complexity can be simplified, 
revealing a relationship where the number of resulting Eisenstein series series 
for the given pair of Eisenstein series is equal to seven, 
with a straightforward cancellation formula identifying one vanishing term 
driven by the constant term at $s=-n$.

Designing effective collision avoidance systems for mobile robots remains a key challenge, especially when accounting for the robot's spatial structure.
In this paper, we develop a novel control approach that leverages Control Barrier Functions and Quadratic Programming to enable safe navigation for mobile robotic arms in cluttered environments, taking their configuration into consideration.
We validate our algorithm through simulations of a free-flying robotic arm and a real-world implementation on an 8-degree-of-freedom robot.

Natural language processing, a crucial field of study, strives to comprehend text via digital analysis, despite the inherent imperfections arising from diverse forms of written and spoken language. This work delves into employing various graph-based methodologies for resolving the challenge of text summarization via a selective extraction technique. Two key indicators – sentence overlap and edit distance – are employed for gauging sentence similarity.

Researchers have suggested the application of quantum interferometry and information processing in Bose-Einstein condensates. However, the current BEC-based interactions are primarily linear and susceptible to noise and disturbances. To develop robust BEQI, it is essential to establish robust, non-linear quantum gates. Our study introduces novel, reliable BEC-based nonlinear gates, specifically a controlled NOT, a controlled phase, and a T gate. These gates are based on the diffusion of BECs through an aperture and can be precisely controlled by an focused laser beam. Our research reveals that the reliability of these quantum gates is significantly improved, reaching error rates as low as $10^{-5}$. Furthermore, we have used these reliable gates to execute a Grover search algorithm, achieving an reliability error of 0.015. Our innovative design of the gate offers the advantage of easy scalability for computational search operations.

This paper aims to accomplish two distinct objectives. Firstly, it seeks to establish a unicity theorem for meromorphic mappings from a complete Kähler manifold to a complex projective space, under the constraint of limited intersection with hypersurfaces. Secondly, the paper aims to prove a unicity theorem for the case of nondegenerate meromorphic mappings that share a specified number of hyperplanes in a particular geometric configuration.

Polynomial system solving plays a crucial role in various applications to capture nonlinear geometric attributes. To obtain a solution set devoid of degeneration, which end-users desire to avoid, the Nondegenerate Locus Computing Problem must be resolved. We introduce a new algorithm to solve this problem, leveraging signature detection of resultants as the core component. On specific systems, this algorithm exhibits superior performance compared to existing methods.

Direct photons have been measured at $p_T<5$ GeV/$c$ for midrapidity and most central events of Cu$+$Cu collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}=200$ GeV. By calculating the $e^{\prime}$ yield by subtracting hadron-photon conversion contributions from photon data and subtracting thermal photon contributions from electron yield, the photon spectra and $d^2N_{el+{\gamma}}/dp_Tdy$ were obtained. Hadron yields for Cu$+$Cu collisions match those of Au$+$Au collisions within two standard deviations, and the electron spectra exceed hadron spectra significantly. Thermal photon yields in Cu$+$Cu collisions exceeded binary scaling times nuclear cross section at $p_T>4$ GeV/$c$, exhibiting more intense emission at lower $p_T$. Integration of thermal photon yield over $p_T$ showed that $p_T<4$ GeV/$c$ contribution significantly exceeds 95% confidence interval beyond binary scaling at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}=200$ GeV.

The Turan tetrahedron problem seeks to calculate the Turan density of the tetrahedron graph K4^3 by finding the maximum l1-norm of a K4^3-free n-vertex 3-uniform hypergraph's codegree vector. We develop a new method for determining hypergraph extremality using the clique sum technique, which is then applied to calculate the Turan density of the tetrahedron graph as the square root of the previously established Danies' lower bound.

Achieving a seamless visual experience and optimal system performance when displaying line joins on vector maps requires an efficient anti-aliasing technique. However, the limitations of OpenGL API hinder optimal rendering results when approximating the anti-aliased effect through multiple triangles. In an attempt to rectify this issue, this study introduces a straightforward yet high-performance algorithm leveraging the drawImage API to achieve efficient anti-aliasing for line joins. Our solution enhances rendering quality by leveraging texture-based rendering and improves system responsiveness by leveraging hardware acceleration. A thorough comparison with existing techniques demonstrates the superior performance of our approach, showcasing reduced system latency and enhanced rendering smoothness. As a outcome, this study contributes to the creation of high-quality vector map rendering and resulting in a smooth user experience.

The multivariate interpolation operator is traditionally accompanied by specific assumptions regarding its chosen interpolation function.  In this paper, a novel interpolation function is defined using the exponential e to the power of x, and it is shown that the resulting operator preserves both the values and derivatives of given bivariate data.  The proof relies on the means value theorem, and subsequently, the operator is applied to approximate data without requiring any particular smoothness or periodicity.  Moreover, the convergence of the operator is proven under the conditions that the given data are smooth and its step size is sufficiently small.  These results are supported by accompanying examples.

Pulsar halos are large-scale, high-energy emission structures, formed when energetic electrons and positrons break free from pulsar wind nebulae. As a novel category of gamma-ray emitters, pulsar halos serve as optimal probes for examining the diffusion of cosmic rays within the Galaxy's localized areas, as well as their escape from pulsar wind nebulae. Research on pulsar halos has brought to light the distinct diffusion properties that differ from the average rate of pulsar wind electrons' propagation in the Galaxy. This review focuses on observational findings of pulsar halos, their potential explanations, and their significance in understanding cosmic-ray diffusion and pulsar energy release. Furthermore, we explore the pivotal role that future telescopes will play in advancing the study of pulsar halos.

Understanding the relationship between atmospheric conditions is crucial for multiple fields, including multiple weather systems, navigation, and aviation. Although identifying simple species of weather is a well-studied topic, recognizing complex and composite species remains a significant challenge. In this study, we introduce the first multi-class dataset comprising complex and composite weather species, accompanied by an in-depth analysis of the effectiveness of existing convolutional neural network approaches. Furthermore, we introduce an innovative method for optimizing network performance that involves integrating multiple sub-networks trained on diverse subsets of the training data. This method yields superior results, demonstrating the potential for improved performance with only a minimal increase in computational resources.

Our analysis examines how climate change interest shifts among diverse groups and how their individual interests interconnect. Initially, we track the individual trends, followed by developing a cross-influence model that we then validate using a VAR model. Our results indicate significant fluctuations in the general public's climate change interest, as well as in the behaviors of scientists, environmental institutions, and economists towards the issue. Moreover, we find that the individual interests have mutual effects on each other, and a one-step lagging influence is observed.

Soft grippers are increasingly utilized across various applications, thanks to their versatility and scalability, which are enabled by their material properties. However, their nonlinear dynamics are complicated and difficult to understand, largely due to the influence of deformation rates and path history. This research introduces a data-driven, real-time modeling approach for multi-sensed, soft multi-fingered grippers, using the online-kKRR method and assuming the sufficiency of the Koopman operator in capturing their dynamics, despite numerous research limitations. real-time modeling of the gripper dynamics is achieved through continuous modeling, which in turn facilitates the use of model-predictive control for optimizing grip quality. This study also reports successful outcomes of the proposed approach in addressing the online-identification challenges associated with the gripper's multibody dynamics.

One of the fundamental problems in science and engineering involves finding the lowest cost value for a given function through the parameters. Numerous optimization techniques have been developed to solve this problem, yet they generally require the cost function to have specific differentiable and smooth properties. In contrast, in Machine Learning, the parameters reside on a manifold with a distinct geometric structure derived from the training data, whereas the corresponding cost function lacks a clear relationship to this geometric framework. Thus, standard optimization techniques may not effectively exploit the inherent structure of the parameter manifold. Natural gradient descent offers a means to perform optimization on manifold-based parameter spaces by incorporating geometric properties into the relationship between the gradient and parameter changes. We extend NGD to general differentiable cost functions defined on manifold-based parameter spaces equipped with a Riemannian metric and demonstrate its convergence even when the cost function is non-smooth. Moreover, we show that NGD retains a connection to stochastic optimization, yielding similar relationships between the convergence rate and the specific characteristics of the cost function. Our results also encompass the special case of f-divergence minimization problems commonly encountered in Machine Learning. Ultimately, the proposed method enables optimization of loss functions on manifold-based parameter spaces resulting in statistically consistent estimators for well-known estimators such as the maximum likelihood estimator.
